title: Traj-MLLM: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Reform Trajectory Data Mining?

problem.claim: A general model is needed to analyze human trajectories across geographic regions and tasks.

gap.claim: Existing approaches are restricted to specific regions or a limited number of tasks, while trajectory modality gaps hinder task-independent representations and flexible task adaptation.

contributions.claim: Traj-MLLM is a framework that uses multimodal large language models for trajectory data mining.
The framework integrates multiview contexts to convert raw trajectories into interleaved image-text sequences while preserving spatial-temporal characteristics.
A prompt optimization method produces data-invariant prompts for task adaptation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across four publicly available datasets, Traj-MLLM reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by 48.05%, 15.52%, 51.52%, and 1.83% for travel time estimation, mobility prediction, anomaly detection, and transportation mode identification, respectively.
The reported performances do not require training data or fine-tuning of the MLLM backbones.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames general trajectory analysis across regions and tasks as an important application problem.
It identifies limited regional and task generalization and foundational modality and adaptation challenges.
It proposes Traj-MLLM, combining multiview image-text trajectory representations, MLLM reasoning, and prompt optimization.
The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on four trajectory-mining tasks without training data or MLLM backbone fine-tuning.

source_observation.claim: The approach combines multiview context encoding with data-invariant prompt optimization for adapting one MLLM-based framework across trajectory tasks.

interpretation.claim: Separating modality representation from task adaptation may support broader reuse of a general trajectory-analysis model.

application.claim: For multimodal domain data, represent domain-specific inputs in a form usable by a general model and use task-level prompting to reduce task-specific adaptation.

exception.claim: The supplied units do not establish effectiveness beyond the reported datasets, regions, or four tasks.

unknowns: The four dataset names and their geographic coverage are not supplied.
The baseline identities and evaluation protocols are not supplied.
The meaning and denominator of the reported percentage improvements are not specified.
The prompt optimization procedure and multiview representation details are not specified.
Ablation results and independent verification are not supplied.
